newsitem.title: UK: SCOT MEDIA AIMS FOR GRAMPIAN BENEFITS.
newsitem.headline: SCOT MEDIA AIMS FOR GRAMPIAN BENEFITS.

text.p: Scottish Media Group Plc, which on Thursday lifted its stake in Ulster Television Plc to almost 15 percent, said its priority was to integrate its new Grampian Television unit.
"Our priority is to bed in Grampian and get returns for shareholders (on the deal)," Scottish Media Finance Director Gary Hughes told a telephone conference call.
Scottish Media's acquisition of Grampian in a 105 million stg agreed deal went unconditional on Wednesday.

Hughes said Scottish, which on Thursday agreed to buy a 13.1 percent chunk of Ulster for 14.13 million stg, would consider increasing its stake further if stock became available at the right price, citing the 205p which Scottish has paid. But he stressed that Scottish had no current plans to make an offer for Ulster.

Hughes said the Ulster stake would help to prevent the ITV commercial TV network from becoming too biased towards London-based companies. He said Ulster and Scottish both enjoyed distinct identities, separate regional economies and high levels of brand awareness.

Asked why Scottish had not sought a deal with Border Television, its small southern neighbour, Hughes noted that only one third of Border's viewers actually live in Scotland. The rest are on the English side of the dividing line.
ITV, which comprises a patchwork of 15 regional broadcasters, is in the process of consolidating after a two-licence ownership cap was lifted.
Scottish Media has taken advantage of the new rules to add Grampian, which covers the city of Aberdeen and northern Scotland, to its existing licence for the densely populated central Scotland area.
ITV in England and Wales is being carved up by Carlton Communications Plc, Granada Group Plc and United News & Media Plc.
